criteria.evidence: "It matters to software delivery planning because that domain turns a business intent into work that agents can build. This capability is where those business intents and the model come from." "What makes it unique: it starts from something that works, not from a written spec."
"The reason: the Source must outlive the link or the file." "The reason: a model drawn from a source nobody read has no basis." "Other parts may already rely on these pages."

"Specify intents (fn-specify-intents): drafts one business intent for each need the product meets, and the person confirms or drops each one." "Specify capabilities (fn-specify-capabilities): writes a full page for each capability and creates its features with their pages."

"Out: choosing what to build first. Later shaping work picks the features a person can test end to end and turns them into work items." "Never: set a capability to active, or rank one part above another. Ranking belongs to the later shaping work, and no step sets a capability active today."

"Who it serves: the product owner, who wants to confirm what a product is for without writing a spec first." "How we will know: a new builder, who never saw the prototype, builds the product from the intents and the model alone." "Out: keeping intents up to date as the product changes. This capability does not do it, and no capability in the model owns it yet."
